explanations: M.2 keying determines physical and protocol compatibility. B+M keyed drives (typically SATA) fit in both B-keyed and M-keyed slots due to having two notches. NVMe drives with only an M key will not fit in a B-keyed slot because the single notch is in the wrong position. An M-keyed slot can accept both M-keyed NVMe and B+M keyed SATA drives physically, though the slot must support the protocol. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (M.2 form factors, NVMe vs SATA, keying).

Boot Option #1 determines which device the system tries first during POST. To boot from USB, change Boot Option #1 from Hard Drive to USB Device. Fast Boot skips some POST checks for speed. CSM enables legacy BIOS compatibility for older OS installations. Network Stack controls PXE booting. Review: Chapter 1, Motherboards, Processors, and Memory (BIOS/UEFI configuration, boot order, POST sequence).

ipconfig /flushdns purges the local DNS resolver cache, forcing the machine to query the DNS server for fresh records on the next lookup. Windows caches DNS responses to speed up repeated lookups, but stale entries can cause connectivity issues after server IP changes. After flushing, use nslookup to verify the new IP resolves correctly. Review: Chapter 6, TCP/IP and Wireless (DNS caching, ipconfig switches, name resolution).

Modern PSUs include dedicated PCIe power cables in 6-pin and 8-pin (6+2) configurations specifically for graphics cards. The 6+2 design allows the same cable to fit either a 6-pin or 8-pin socket. Molex adapters are a last resort and can be unreliable. The 24-pin ATX powers the motherboard, and EPS 12V powers the CPU. Neither should be repurposed for GPU power. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (PSU connectors, PCIe power, wattage requirements).

A new drive appears as "Not Initialized" in Disk Management because it has no partition table. Right-click the disk label and choose "Initialize Disk," then select GPT (for UEFI systems and drives over 2 TB) or MBR (for legacy BIOS). After initialization, create a volume and format it. The existing Disk 0 partitions (Windows, Recovery, EFI) are already healthy. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (disk initialization, GPT vs MBR, Disk Management).

shutdown /r performs a restart (/r = reboot). The /t 0 flag sets the timeout to zero seconds, causing an immediate restart without the default 30-second countdown. This is essential when administering machines remotely because the default delay can be confusing. Other useful switches: /s for shutdown, /f to force-close applications, /o to boot to Advanced Startup Options. Review: Chapter 9, Software Troubleshooting (shutdown command, Windows recovery, remote administration).

WPA3-Personal replaces the WPA2 4-way handshake with SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals), also known as Dragonfly. SAE is a zero-knowledge proof protocol that prevents captured handshakes from being used in offline brute-force or dictionary attacks. WPA2-PSK is vulnerable because the 4-way handshake can be captured and cracked offline. WEP is fundamentally broken. WPA2-Enterprise avoids shared keys but does not solve the protocol-level weakness. Review: Chapter 6, TCP/IP and Wireless (WPA3, SAE, wireless security protocols).

A down-arrow icon in Device Manager means the device has been manually disabled. This can happen accidentally via keyboard shortcut, a user disabling it to save battery, or group policy. Right-click the device and select "Enable device" to restore functionality. This is different from a yellow triangle (driver problem) or a red X (device error). Bluetooth is commonly toggled off on laptops, so always check Device Manager when pairing fails. Review: Chapter 10, Mobile Devices (Bluetooth, Device Manager status icons, enabling/disabling hardware).

Within diskpart, the "format" command formats the currently selected volume. "fs=ntfs" specifies the NTFS file system (standard for Windows data drives). "quick" performs a quick format that writes a new file table without scanning every sector, completing in seconds rather than hours for large drives. A full format also checks for bad sectors. After formatting, use "assign" to give the volume a drive letter. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (diskpart, formatting, NTFS, file systems).

Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors like VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V Server, and Citrix XenServer run directly on hardware with no host OS, providing the best performance and direct resource allocation for VMs. Type 2 hypervisors (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation) run on top of a host OS, adding overhead. Docker uses OS-level containerization, not full hardware virtualization. Windows Sandbox is a lightweight, non-persistent isolated environment. Review: Chapter 7, Virtualization and Cloud (Type 1 vs Type 2 hypervisors, VM resource management).
